Chelameswar, Justice Ranjan Gogoi, Justice Madan Lokur and Justice Kurien Joseph) had to come forward and address a press conference differing with the views of Supreme Court. They said they had given a letter to the Chief Justice two months back in connection with the functioning of Chief Justice of India. They even said that they would place these matters before the people i.e. to save the democracy of the country. The main issue is with regard to the death of Justice Loya, a CBI Judge who was hearing a case of encounter killing and it was also connected with Shri Amit Shah, All India President of BJP. I don’t want to go into the details here. Such a very serious case was transferred to a bench of junior Justice. This is one of the issues raised by these Justices. But in the speech made by our President, nothing is said about this very serious issue of judiciary.

The burning issue of common people in India is the price rise. This government has failed to control the price rise though they had promised it in their election manifesto and earlier in the budget speeches. The main reason for the price rise is the uncontrolled prices of the petroleum and diesel. In the international market, the price of crude oil has come down drastically. 

The benefit of this price reduction is not transferred to the common people. The Government has increased excise duty 17 times. That is the main reason for the price rise of essential commodities. But, as a result, prices of almost all essential commodities have gone up. Since the excise duty imposed benefits has gone to the oil companies. But nothing is mentioned about this price rise which is the common man's issue in the speech delivered by our President. 

When the NDA Government came to power they promised that 2 crores jobs would be given to the unemployed youth. Four years have passed, 8 crore jobs has to be given by the Government according to their promise. But only 8 lakhs employment opportunities have been created. So, the claim of the President that his Government is going to give more jobs to the youth is baseless. 

The other major issue of the nation is the farmers’ suicide and their problems. Hon. President said that in the year 2022 the income of the farmers would be doubled. It is surprised to note that the period of this Government is going to expire within one year. So, what is the right of this Government to speak about the year 2022? Government has to take immediate steps to give relief to the farmers and write off their loans, which is one of the reasons for the suicides of the farmers. Now, they promised 50% of the MSP of coast of production but in their election manifesto they had said they would be ready to give 150% of MSP but the same has not been implemented. So, the promise is made with regard to the farmer's welfare is not convincing. 

Hon. President said much about the welfare of the women, but not a single word is used with regard to the Women Reservation Bill which is pending. Government got the highest majority, then what is the reason for not bringing the promised Reservation Bill. It shows that baseless and hollowness promises to women. Every day we hear about attacks on women and children, but what concrete action Government has taken. Nirbhaya Fund is not spent and Nirbhaya Centres haven't opened in various parts of the country. 

SCs/STs and other backward sections have been neglected for a long time. The allocation of SCs/STs is only 1.6% of the GDP, but their population is 25%. This is another valid example of their attitude towards SCs and STs. 

In recent times, our nation faced serious attacks against the secular ideas and organizations. The famous writer Shri Kalburgi, Vice Chancellor of Karnataka University, the progressive writer Shri Pansare and Shri Narendra Dabodkar, the journalists, Gauri Lankesh and many other scholars and writers were threatened and even killed. This is really a challenge before our nation. But, it is unfortunate that President is silent about these serious issues. 

The figures quoted by our Hon'ble President with regard to the economic growth are unrealistic. The demonetization and GST have weakened our economy as pointed out by many of the great economists and political leaders, but Government is not ready to recognize these mistakes. Growth rate has gone down, inflation is increasing. The gap between the poor and the rich is widening. Though Government say that we are going towards a new India and glittering India, but result is negative. 

So, while I welcome the President's Speech, I reserve my criticisms.

*श्री रवीद्र कुमार पाण्डेय (गिरिडीह) : मैं आदरणीय राष्‍ट्रपति  महोदय के अभिभाषण  के पक्ष में अपने विचार व्‍यक्‍त करना चाहता हूं।

महामहिम ने अपने अभिभाषण  का प्रारंभ इस सरकार की संविधान के प्रति प्रतिबद्धता को बताते हुए किया है। बाबा साहेब की सामाजिक एवं आर्थिक जनतंत्र को अमली जामा यही सरकार पहना रही है।

स्वच्छता अभियान में शत-प्रतिशत घरों में शौचालय एवं घर-घर में "उज्जवला योजना" के तहत एलपीजी, महिला सशक्तिकरण एवं सामाजिक जनतंत्र का द्योतक है। महिला स्वाबलंबन एवं देश की आधा आबादी के चहुमुंखी विकास के लिए सरकार प्रतिबद्ध है।

सदियों से इस देश में हमारी मुसलमान बहनें "तीन तलाक" से सतायी जा रही थीं। धार्मिक तुष्‍टिकरण के नाम पर पिछली कई सरकारें इस मुद्दे पर चुप्पी साधे थीं। इस सरकार ने "वाक द टाक" को सही साबित करते हुए,"तीन तलाक" के खिलाफ बिल लाया है। महिला-सशक्तिकरण का इससे बड़ा उदाहरण क्या हो सकता है। एनडीए की इस सरकार ने महिलाओं के उत्थान में, प्रगति में कोई भेदभाव नहीं किया है। "बेटी बचाओ, बेटी-पढ़ाओ" ने आंदोलन का रूप ले लिया है। बेटियां मुफ्त साइकिल, मुफ्त ड्रेस एवं मुफ्त किताबों के साथ स्कूल की पढ़ाई कर रही हैं। मैटरनिटी बेनेफिट एक्ट का संशोधन कर छुट्टी को 12 हफ्ते से 26 हफ्ते कर दिया गया है।

आदरणीय राष्‍ट्रपति  महोदय ने इस सरकार की किसानों के प्रति दायित्व निर्वहन को बताया है। किसान इस सरकार के मूल सोच में हैं। उनकी प्रगति, उनकी मदद, उनकी समस्याओं का निदान सरकार की प्रमुख मंशा है। किसानों की वार्ऐिाक आय को दोगुना करने के लिए सरकार प्रतिबद्ध है। "प्रधानमंत्री किसान संपदा योजना", "जन-धन योजना" एवं "प्रधानमंत्री मुद्रा योजना" मील के पत्थर साबित हुए हैं। जिस यूरिया के लिए किसान मारे-मारे फिरते थे, इस सरकार ने कभी यूरिया की कमी नहीं होने दी है।

पिछली सरकारों में गरीब एवं किसान, बीमा का प्रीमियन नहीं दे सकते थे। इस सरकार ने 1 रुपया प्रतिमाह की योजना लागू की - प्रधानमंत्री जी के "सुरक्षा बीमा योजना", "जीवन ज्योति योजना" एवं "फसल बीमा योजना" ने किसानों एवं गरीबों के लिए सुरक्षा कवच का काम किया है।

राष्‍ट्रपति  जी ने इस सरकार के "एकात्म मानव-वाद" के प्रति समर्पण को दोहराया है। प्रातः स्मरणीय पं. दीनदयाल उपाध्याय जी के गरीबों एवं पिछड़े वर्ग के उत्थान के सोच को यह सरकार साकार कर रही है। "सौभाग्य योजना" से बिजली, "ग्राम सड़क योजना" का फैलाव एवं "खाद्य सुरक्षा योजना" का ठीक तरीके से अनुपालन गरीब तबके के प्रति सरकार की सर्वोच्च प्राथमिकता दर्शाती है।

सरकार ने अल्पसंख्यकों के तुष्‍टिकरण एवं उन्हें वोट के लिए डरा कर इस्तेमाल करने वाली राजनीति को ठेंगा दिखाया है एवं उन्हें आर्थिक विकास, सशक्तिकरण एवं स्वाबलंबन के रास्ते पर बढ़ने में मदद दी है। ""नई रोशनी"", ""सीखो और कमाओ"" जैसे स्कीम जबरदस्त लोकप्रिय हैं।

राष्‍ट्रपति  महोदय ने इस सरकार की आम-जन, गरीब तबके, व्यापारी तबके, कामकाजी लोग, सभी को साथ लेकर चलने की प्रतिबद्धता को दोहराया है।

यह सरकार ""एक-भारत, श्रेष्ठ-भारत"" के परचम को दुनिया में लहराने में सक्षम है, सतत प्रयत्नशील है। भारत के हर तबके के लोग, हर धर्म के लोग, हर प्रांत के लोग, इस सरकार के साथ हैं - चुनावी विजय-रथ इसका प्रमाण है।

जय हिंद।

*SHRIMATI MEENAKASHI LEKHI (NEW DELHI): To eradicate discrimination against daughters, my Government had introduced the 'Beti Bachao Beti Padhao' scheme. Seeing its positive results, the scheme has been extended from 161 districts to 640 districts. Beti Bachao Beti Padhao scheme that addresses the issue of declining Child Sex Ratio, is yielding encouraging results. Beti Bachao Beti Padhao (BBBP) is currently being implemented in select 161 districts. 

The Government has also taken a big step by amending the Maternity Benefit Act. It now provides for 26 weeks of paid leave in place of 12 weeks. Working women will now be able to devote more time towards their new born children during their crucial formative years. 

Under the Sukanya Samridhi Yojana, launched with an objective of ensuring a secure future to girls, over one crore accounts have been opened and an amount of over Rs. 11,000 crore has been deposited. As per the latest data, on July 21, 2017, 1.1 crore accounts have been opened with deposits amounting to Rs. 15,849 crore. 

My Government has tabled a Bill on Triple Talaq in Parliament. I hope that the Parliament will soon pass it into a law. The law on Triple Talaq, once enacted, will also enable Muslim sisters and daughters to live a life of self-respect with courage. 

Keeping in mind the objective of women's empowerment, for the first time since independence, the restriction on women above 45 years of age to perform Haj Pilgrimage unaccompanied by their male relatives has been removed. This year, more than 1300 women are going on Haj pilgrimage without Mehram.

Launched on May 1st in Ballia, Uttar Pradesh, the Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY) scheme aims to provide clean cooking gas via free LPG connections to 50 million BPL women, with 15 million connections to be provided within the current financial year. "I am sure all of us remember seeing women burning wood to cook food. They and their children had to go through the pain of breathing polluted air. My Government has started the scheme of Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY) which has till date provided 3,30,00,000 free liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) connections to below poverty line (BPL) women."

The President has also talked about the Government working towards providing ample maternity leave to pregnant women. 

Highlighting financial restructuring in favour of women, Hon. President said, "In 2012, there were only 28% women-held saving accounts which have increased to 40% now. 

We need to uplift our women. The country has taken up schemes to promote the usage of toilets. My Government has formulated policies to help construct common as well as private toilets in the rural areas. This not only helps the country in being cleaner but provides a sense of social justice to a woman.

The Government has also set a target of providing of 2 crore toilets under the Swachh Bharat Mission in 2018-19 which directly impact the safety of women and girls. 

SHRI BHARTRUHARI MAHTAB (CUTTACK): Hon. Deputy Speaker, I stand here today to participate in the discussion started on the Motion of Thanks on the President’s Address by my friend Shri Rakesh Singh. Those four lines of the Motion, the keyword is ‘We are deeply grateful to the President for the Address which he has been pleased to deliver in both the Houses of Parliament assembled together on 29th January’. We have to express our deep gratefulness to the hon. President. As the Address itself is the policy statement of this Government, therefore, we always delve into the policy that this Government has been propounding during the last so many years. But what has happened this year is that, on 29th January, the hon. President delivered the speech addressing both the Houses and on 1st February, the hon. Finance Minister has delivered the Budget. So, therefore, today, you must have encountered that the large number of hon. Members, who have spoken before me, have intertwined the Address of the hon. President along with the speech of the hon. Finance Minister. I will try to confine myself only with the speech of the hon. President because we will be discussing for about twelve hours hopefully on the Budget itself.

Before, I delve into the specific paragraphs, I have selected some points for my deliberation. But before I go into these paragraphs, one thing that struck me in the Central Hall is relating to what he mentioned about ‘Adivasi Swatantrata Sangram Sanghrahalaya’. We have seldom deliberated and discussed the fight that our tribal people have fought during the freedom struggle. Very rarely, we have put up memorials for them. But, at least, in this speech, something has been mentioned. How it is going to be developed is what we will see in the future course of action. But one thing is that Kevadia, Gujarat, on the banks of Narmada where the beginning will start, and the proposal of Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Andhra Pradesh, Kerala, Manipur and other States are also under consideration. 

I am reminded of the struggle in Odisha. In erstwhile Bonai State, today’s Sundargarh District, the British soldiers wanted to recruit tribals for Second World War. The tribals who were forcefully being recruited resisted. There was a large-scale fight then and hundreds of tribals were butchered. It is called Amco-Simco agitation. The leader was Nirmal Munda. A group of people even today observe his martyrdom day. Very rarely the government machinery is involved in it. My question here is, is it only confined to the Munda tribe? Odisha Government of course is doing something for that. But here is a fit case for the Union Government to step in, erect a memorial and support an annual festival over there.

There was also a tribal leader in his middle age who had never seen Gandhiji, never heard Gandhiji but was so committed to the ideals Gandhiji propagated that he took part in the struggle and led an agitation for Quit India Movement. He was hauled up by the police; a false case was registered against him and he was hanged to death in 1943. That tribal leader’s name is Laxman Naik. We observe his martyrdom day but he seldom finds place in the national history of freedom struggle. We have to find out about such people and we have to commemorate their sacrifices. I would like to remind this House that Laxman Naik was the only freedom fighter who was hanged to death in 1943.

Hon. President has said, “Nation building is a continuous process in which each citizen of the country has a role to play.” Wise words, no doubt! When Benjamin Franklin was asked a question, “What have we got - a Republic or a Monarchy?” he reportedly replied, “A Republic, if you can keep it.” It was as much a comment on ability as it was on intent. Today I may say a Republic was easy to form even in those turbulent years when this country attained freedom, but we are finding it difficult to sustain. A Republic has to be sustained in content. Our founding fathers gave us a republican Constitution but they hoped for a civic rule necessary for republicanism to strike roots. Did not Dr. Ambedkar warn that however good a Constitution may be, it is sure to turn out bad because those who are called to work it are a bad lot? He did not refer to elected representatives alone but to the incomplete project of transforming people into citizens.

The concern hon. President expressed while speaking to the nation on the eve of this year’s Republic Day and subsequently while addressing the joint session of the two Houses the other day is, “It is our responsibility to exhibit exemplary conduct before the nation. Nation Building is our collective responsibility.” These are the words of the hon. President. What we see today, what we hear today is majoritarianism, rise of vigilantism, institutional corrosion, etc. A democracy gets converted into a show of numerical strength! The capacity to negotiate and deliberate drowns under the noise of numbers. This gives way to anarchic articulation of vigilantism, rejecting the idea of rule of law. I need not explain what has happened in between; some Members have already done that. Both a cause and an effect of this is the all-round corrosion of institutions. 

Do we not find a competition – this is the sad part of it – among institutions to display their flair for failure?

The hon. President in his Address has reminded the nation about working towards achieving robust and inclusive development. NITI – we call it Niti Aayog in Hindi – was formed by the present Government when it came to power in 2014 by dismantling the Planning Commission. The idea was that it would facilitate the State Government and the Union Government to formulate their own plans and programmes and that it would act as a think tank but I would not comment what tank it has become today. Now it is behaving in an arbitrary way. They are insulting the States. A glaring example is that they are identifying 115 districts as most backward districts and asking the States to sign MoUs with NITI. Odisha, Kerala and West Bengal have protested to this.

As per the Constitution, distribution of power, development is not in the domain of the Union Government. Why would this Government unilaterally declare some districts as most backward and send prabharis? From where does this word come? We have heard ‘prabhari’ in some organisations. We have heard about prabharis being deputed by some political parties. But now we have prabharis from NITI and from the Union Government going to the States. Who has coined this word? You are sending prabharis to monitor the development works in the said districts thereby bypassing the Chief Secretary and Secretaries of other related Departments? What is happening in this country?

These 115 districts include 30 districts which are focussed by NITI; 50 backward districts selected by an Inter-Ministerial Committee of Officers; and another 35 districts which have been shortlisted by the Ministry of Home Affairs which are affected by left wing extremism. Where are the States? Neither have they been consulted; nor any inputs were sought from the States. So much about the so-called ‘co-operative federalism’. Shri Kalyan Banerjee has just left. I am sure my friend Shri Jithender Reddy will talk about it. Odisha has not participated in this adventure; so also, Kerala and West Bengal have not participated.

Take the case of Bundelkhand where only one district of that region has been included in this programme, in this idea, in U.P. It is a State ruled by BJP. This demonstrates the lackadaisical manner in which these districts have been selected. Now, it finds place in the Budget Speech of the Minister of Finance. No BJP Chief Minister or Government has the spine to raise objection to this hara-kiri of the Constitution.

What we believe in the Biju Janata Dal is that when you keep the people first it is good politics. My Chief Minister, the leader of the Biju Janata Dal, Shri Naveen Patnaik, says, ‘When you keep people first, there is no anti-incumbency.’ Half a century ago, one of the greatest visionary leaders, Martin Luther King Jr. had said, ‘You cannot lead people unless you love them.’ This, to him, is the guiding philosophy. According to him, ‘If you love your people, you would not see the post you hold as a post but as a means to serve the people; you would not see power as power but as a means to transform the lives of people.’ ‘All the negative associates of politics’ – these are the words which my Chief Minister has said – ‘power, wealth, and position, dissolve into nothingness if you love the people.’ If you work for the people, even in the worst natural disaster, you aim for zero casualty and you end up setting global standards. 

If you love your people, you do not want anyone without a roof over their head and you end up leading the country in rural housing. If you love your people, you will walk an extra mile to include the most vulnerable sections in your growth story and you end up with the path breaking initiative of setting up Tribal Development Council. If you love your people, you do not want hungry stomachs staring into the night and you end up with the highest poverty reduction in the country. If you love your people, you do not fight for elections, you fight for change and transformation. If you love your people with every intent, every step, every action, every signature and with every breath you will work for them. That is the reason why Odisha stands apart from many of the States, especially those that are ruled by the Treasury Benches.

Many leaders go to Odisha saying that सत्रह साल हो गया, अठारह साल हो गया, क्या हुआ? I will just give some instances. With regard to rural housing, 14 lakh pucca houses have been constructed in rural Odisha since 2014. The source of this information is the Rural Development Ministry of the Government of India. Odisha is the pioneering State in India which has distributed 6,11,000 acres of land to 4,11,000 individuals rights, title holders and 3,28,000 acres of land to 5,964 community rights, title holders under the landmark legislation of the Scheduled Tribes and other Traditional Forest Dwellers as on 31st October, 2017. The source of this information is the Report of the Ministry of Tribal Affairs of the Government of India.

We started Mamata Programme to support the pregnant women. Subsequently, year before last, the Janani Programme was initiated by the Union Government. It is a flagship programme of Odisha Government which was launched in 2011 and has benefited more than 30,57,000 women in the State. About 5,63,000 Self Help Groups with more than 67 lakh women have been formed under mission Shakti. Based on NSSO Situation Assessment survey for 2012-13 and 2002-03, farmers’ income doubled in real income terms. राधा मोहन सिंह जी ध्‍यान से सुनिए, हमने किसानों की आय डबल कर दी। Odisha is the top performer with a CAGR of 8.3 per cent. The source is NSSO Situation Assessment Survey of 2012-13. और करना बाकी है।

कृषि और किसान कल्‍याण मंत्री (श्री राधा मोहन सिंह):  जो इसे नहीं मानते हैं उनको समझाइए।

SHRI BHARTRUHARI MAHTAB : In terms of PDS contribution, Odisha is the third highest contributor for food grain procurement in the country in the year 2015-16. It contributes 10.28 per cent of the total procurement in the country. It contributes 26 lakh metric tonne in the year 2015-16. This contribution was only 2.07 per cent in 2002-03. The source of this information is a Lok Sabha Starred Question of 26th April, 2016.

Poverty has declined.As per the household consumer expenditure data of NSS up to 2011-12, poverty in rural Odisha has declined by 24.6 per cent. इस तरह एक-एक करके डिफरेंट पैरामीटर्स पर जाएं तो काफी जानकारी मिलेगी जो लोग पॉलिटीकल स्‍टंट के हिसाब से कहते हैं कि 17 सालों में क्‍या हुआ। नवीन पटनायक जी ने करके दिखा दिया बीजू जनता दल ने करके दिखा दिया। Therefore, incumbency is not a factor. We do our work because we love our people.

Odisha’s GDP growth rate was 7.94 per cent in 2016-17 in comparison to India’s GDP growth rate of 7.1 per cent in the same year. But there are other issues which need to be flagged and one major issue is Mahanadi. हमने पिछले सेशन में बार-बार कहा, रिक्‍वेस्‍ट की, प्‍लीड किया, आर्ग्‍यू किया कि ट्रिब्‍युनल बनाइए। मेरा वाटर रिसोर्स मिनिस्‍टर के लिए पूरा सम्‍मान है, वह कर पाएंगे, लेकिन मालूम नहीं, why was he advised in such a way but at least he committed himself in this House that he will make the Tribunal in three months. The matter was pending in the Supreme Court. You had given an affidavit in which you have gone back on your words and said that you will form a Tribunal. But again you gave an affidavit in the Supreme Court saying that it is not feasible. यहां फिर कहा कि तीन महीने में बनाएंगे। सुप्रीमकोर्ट ने क्‍या कहा, सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने कहा कि एक महीने में ट्रिब्‍युनल बनाओ। 

What progress has been made? Mahanadi River water dispute is a dispute on which the apex court has already pronounced its decision and had admonished this Government for going back on its words to form the Tribunal. It had asked the Union Government to do it within one month’s time. This was pronounced on 23rd January, 2018 and today is 6th February, 2018. How many days have passed? Today is the 15th day to be precise. Has any step been taken? Does this not show the brazenness in which the Government treats the pronouncement of the Supreme Court of India? Does this not demonstrate the partisan attitude of this Government towards Odisha?

We will wait for the decision of the Tribunal. We are sure it will give a decision in our favour because of the illegality of the construction of the upstream of Mahanadi by Chhattisgarh. But the Union Government which was expected to function in a neutral way is becoming partisan. Why do you not form a Tribunal? Why do you wait for the single unitary tribunal which is still in the womb? Whom are you befooling? The Chief Minister of Odisha on 2nd February, 2018 has again written a letter to the Prime Minister but there is no response. I can only plead in this House for the wisdom of all Members and ask is this the way the Union Government should function? How partisan have you become just because you are going to face elections in some months’ time in Chhattisgarh.

The dams are being constructed illegally. Water has been stopped illegally and Odisha is being bereft. What are we asking for? We are asking for a tribunal. At least, tribunal will give a judgment. It will hear both the sides. We have pleaded before the Union Government not to be partisan and you take a decision. The previous Minister said that he has no power. At least, now the

Supreme Court has given you instructions and said as per the constitutional provision a tribunal has to be formed. But I am sorry to mention that the Government is yet to proceed.

We have heard about triple talaq in the Address of the hon. President. He expressed hope that the Bill will be passed. He will act as per the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers. Triple Talaq Bill has already been passed by this House and it goes against the verdict of the Supreme Court. Talaq-e-Biddat is unconstitutional. There is a need to have a law pronouncing Talaq-e-Biddat as unlawful. We are not against that but the Bill which is pending in the Rajya Sabha needs thorough correction. That Bill to do away with instant talaq is on the way of instant law. A law made in a hurry is bound to be faulty. Can you not incorporate in nikahnama that the Talaq-e-Biddat is not allowed. Can a separation/divorce be on record? If marriages fail, should Governments jail husbands? Marriages are social contracts. There should always be attempt for reconciliation. If the husband is put behind bars on the complaint alone, will there be any scope of reconciliation? The Bill is meant to protect the interest of Muslim women. Have they been consulted in any form before the preparation of this Bill which is a must as per the provision before law making?

Any law, before it is made, has to be consulted with the respective stakeholders. That is the practice and provision of the Constitution. The Government has prepared a Bill which is half-baked. This will bring more disaster to the womenfolk of Muslim community than empowering them. I fail to understand as to why the Government is doing it. Congress Government committed a mistake in 1986 and now this Government is committing another mistake. The Government may correct it and bring another amendment removing the penal provision. Let the Government not become adamant.

My friend Shri A.P. Jithender Reddy has come out openly about holding simultaneous elections about which the hon. President has spoken and the hon. Prime Minister also has expressed his views positively. The other young `Prasad’, Shri Ravi Shankar Prasad from Bihar, our hon. Law Minister, is going around the country saying that we should debate this. I may remind Shri Reddy, my friend, that all these talks of holding simultaneous elections started from the dinner table that both of us shared once with the hon. Prime Minister. It has rolled on since 2014, where hon. Deputy-Speaker, Sir, was also present, in different forums. The Election Commission also has come out with an opinion. What is the opinion of the Election Commission? Article 83, article 85, article 172, article 174 and article 356 of the Indian Constitution need to be amended for fixing Lok Sabha and Assembly terms. If today it has found place in the Address of the hon. President, should we not be told about the Government’s view? Why does the Government not prepare a draft and circulate it? Today is the time of the social media, but what is the view of the Government? What is the opinion of the Government. The Government is asking others to debate and discuss the matter. Why does the Government not come out with a draft on this? Let that be the basis on which discussions will take place. The Standing Committee earlier had given a report. If you want further discussion on this issue, let us understand as to what the Government intends to do. Why does the Government not prepare a draft and circulate it basing on which debates and discussions will take place? What is the point of this wishful thinking?

Hon. Deputy-Speaker, Sir, the hon. President mentioned about the presence of Heads of States of ASEAN countries during this year’s Republic Day celebrations. It is indeed a special dimension to our world vision. But does it end here? What I have understood is that the principal gain of the ASEAN-Indian Commemorative Summit is to provide for an ample clarity on what our partnerships have achieved and where it should move in the future. As the celebrations and the colourful spectacles have ended, is it not time to begin the hard work? When you stand at the peak of a mountain, you get full view of the path travelled and the road ahead that will take you to the next peak. It is now time to draw up a to-do list? Have the Government prepared it? You have a huge responsibility to shoulder.

Republics crumble when Statesmanship stops at showmanship; politics breed fear and institutions fail to strengthen norms and procedures. Recently we celebrated our 68th Republic Day, seven decades of enjoying the Republic, the fortresses of communities have become more impenetrable. In today’s India nobody can criticise, comment or censure the practices of another community of which she or he is not part of.

Communities are beyond debate and criticism. Relations among communities are also marked by mutual suspicion. Caste-community based separation, suspicion and violence ensure that the idea of citizenship become a chimera. Then how can we conceive the idea of public good that would emerge and sustain in a republic? That is the fundamental question before us today.

Given the fragmentation of the public and impossibility of common good, all politics and policy making is taking the form of a cynical exercise of balancing competing expectations. Serious casualty in this process is the loss of the idea of common good which is at the core of a republic. Does this Government has any roadmap to build in citizenship, collective responsibility and strive for common cause and public good? The answer is there for everyone to see. How social justice and economic democracy has been strengthened is pouring out in the newspapers daily.

The last suggestion that I would like to make today is, our Constitution is instructive. Cannot we make reading of this text compulsory in the classrooms across the country? This is the Gospel. Constitution is the gospel. Constitution is the Gita and Constitution is the Quran of modern Bharat, Sashakt Bharat and Samudha Bharat.

Vande Utkal Janani, Jai Hind, Jai Jagannath.

*SHRIMATI V. SATHYABAMA (TIRUPUR): I would like to bring to the notice of the Government the long-pending Railway demands of the people of my Tirupur Parliamentary Constituency. The Government should consider and take appropriate steps for speedy execution of the pending demands. 

1- Train No. 22476 Coimbatore-Bikaner express can be operated from Erode or Tirupur instead of Coimbatore. Further this weekly train needs to be converted to a bi-weekly train.

2- Train No. 16614 Coimbatore- Rajkot weekly train to be converted into weekly-twice train. 

3- Mettupalayam-Coimbatore passenger train can be extended up to Tirupur. 

4- Manglaore-Coimbatore fast passenger train can be extended to Tirupur. 

5- Katpadi-Salem MEMU passenger train can be extended up to Tirupur. 

There is an urgent need for introduction of Shuttle Train services between Tirupur and Salem via Erode as well as between Tirupur - Palakkad and Tirupur to Tirucharapalli via Karur. 

It is a long pending demand of the people of my Tirupur constituency that a New Railway line through Mettupalayam to Chennai via Sathyamangalam, Gobichettipalayam and Erode be initiated soon. I take this opportunity to urge the Government to fulfil the Railway demands of the people of Tirupur constituency. 

The much needed Athikadavu-Avinashi Flood Canal Scheme at an estimated cost of Rs. 1862 crores may be sanctioned on a priority basis. This would help the people of the Kongu region to get adequate water for both irrigation and drinking purposes. 

Gunderipallam reservoir is situated across jungle stream near Kongarpalayam village of Gobichettipalayam Taluk in Erode district of Tamil Nadu. The splendid and the spectacular view of the reservoir and surrounding area attract tourists and film shoots often takes place here. I urge the Government to release adequate funds for this purpose so that Gunderipallam Reservoir could become a significant tourist centre. 

In Tirupur, the Postal Department is having a site measuring 1.04 acres and 298sq ft. at Kallampalayam Road. This land is lying vacant for the last several years. Sixteen post offices are located in and around Tirupur within 10 kilometers radius. Rent is being paid for 13 post offices. Though Tirupur head post office is functioning in its own building, it is functioning in a very cramped space. As the building is very old and situated near the railway station, it is not possible to expand Tirupur head post office building either horizontally or vertically. If a new building is constructed, Passport Kendra can also function which will be more convenient to the members of public in and around Tirupur. 

Therefore, I urge the Union Government to allot sufficient funds for construction of an integrated building for the purposes of Department of Posts and Passport Kendra at the vacant site at Kallampalayam Road, Tirupur. 

The Keeripallam Odai and Modachur Pallam Odai rehabilitation works for the benefit of the people of Gobichettipalayam and its surroundings need to be executed under the Flood Management Scheme. Moreover, a Water Treatment Plant also to be provided at the tail end of this Odai so that the treated water could be utilized for agricultural purpose as a recycling process. I urge the Union Government to allocate Rs. 55 crores to expedite this very important Keeripallam Odai and Modachur Pallam Odai rehabilitation works in Tamil Nadu. 

*SHRI T.G. VENKATESH BABU (CHENNAI NORTH): Hon'ble President in his Address has stated that the Government is committed to doubling of farmer's income by 2022. But in reality, the situation is different. Majority of the farmers in the country are living in debt trap. They are not getting timely credit, quality seeds and subsidy. Most often, they are living at the mercy of money lenders and not protected. In Tamil Nadu, as per the 2011 census, nearly 8.67 lakh farmers have quit agriculture and shifted to other sectors during the last 10 years due to various reasons including huge loss. Moreover, the farmers sell their land to real estate and prefer to work on daily wage. The reason attributed for the plight of the farmers is wrong import policy of the Centre, un-remunerative prices for their produce, industrialization and urbanization, coupled with failure to divert the rain and other waters going to sea to the farmers' fields by linking rivers. In addition, the Government should assist the farmers in educating and promoting the cultivation of organic farming. 

I am glad to learn that the present Government is committed to empower people belonging to backward classes by providing constitutional status to the National Commission for Backward Classes. I am sure that the Commission set up to examine the sub-categorization of backward classes would submit its report shortly so that the benefits of higher education and jobs can be availed by the most backward sections among the backward classes. It is pertinent to mention here that the Government should consider extension of the benefits of higher education and jobs to the economically weaker section from the general category also without disturbing the existing set up.

As regards 'Beti Bachao Beti Padhao' Scheme, out of 640 districts in the country, the scheme is extended only to 161 districts and more number of districts are yet to be covered. The scheme faces challenges due to lack of support from civic bodies, constantly changing administration, obsession with marriage, etc. and these issues are to be addressed to achieve to desired results. 

The 'Jan dhan Yojana' of the Government helps the poor to open a bank account on their own. However, on the flipside, privacy and security issues have cropped up, and new light is shed on the scheme's susceptibility to frauds i.e. whether the bank accounts opened are actually being used. Additionally, several features of the schemes remain ambiguous. For instance, the promising overdraft facility is left to the discretion of banks, which creates prejudices as banks will avoid such situations that could potentially lead to NPAs. These issues are to be addressed by the Government and then only fruits of the scheme reach the intended beneficiaries. 

I am sorry to state that the Union Government has recently scrapped the Haj subsidy which was first introduced by the British Government in 1932 for pilgrims as the fund will instead be used for empowerment of minorities for this year. In this connection, I would like to submit that around 1.75 lakh people prefer to go to Haj this year and this decision of the Government will adversely affect their long cherished lifetime dream. At this juncture, I urge upon the Union Government to refrain from the abrupt withdrawal of the subsidy scheme and it can be extended by considering their economic status. 

As regards power sector, I would like to mention about the Kudankulam Nuclear Power Plant (KNPP). Quite often, the two reactors are shut down citing 'Under Maintenance' which has raised safety issues of the project. This has raised concern among the activists that the project was set up with substandard components and needs to put a thorough overhaul. Besides, there is also no clarity of time schedule of the commissioning of Units 3 and 4.

The Government of Tamil Nadu is deeply concerned with the plight of our fishermen who are continuously attacked and detained by the Sri Lankan Navy. It is a regular occurrence throughout the year. Their boats, nets and other fishing vessels are capsized by the Sri Lankan authorities and are damaged. Government is also aware that 163 fishing boats and gear, which are essential for fishermen to earn their humble livelihood, have not yet been released by Sri Lanka. Long periods of disuse and the monsoons have condemned the boats and equipment to ruin and the poor fishermen are being subjected to a huge permanent loss. Government of Tamil Nadu is consistently requesting that the only means of livelihood of our fishermen is returned in a refurbished condition by the Centre at the earliest. Besides, immediate action may be taken through the highest diplomatic channels to secure the release of 108 fishermen and 165 fishing boats, including 8 fishermen and 2 mechanised fishing boats which were apprehended on 25.01.2016. Recently, in the early hours of 25-01-2018, it has been reported that 8 fishermen along with their 2 mechanised fishing boats set out for fishing from Jegathapattinam fishing base of Pudukkottai District have been apprehended by the Sri Lankan Navy and taken to Sri Lanka.

Besides, there are implications of a new Bill introduced in the Sri Lankan Parliament on 24th January, 2018 with provisions to impose huge penalties on Indian fishermen, who engage in legitimate fishing in their traditional fishing grounds of Palk Bay. New amendments made in the Fisheries and Aquatic Resources Act, 1960 of Sri Lanka during the year 2017 has banned and declared bottom trawling as a punishable offence. In addition, a new Bill named the Foreign Fishing Vessels Bill, has also been approved by the Sri Lankan Cabinet which provides for stringent penalties against fishing in the sovereign territory of Sri Lanka. It is widely reported in the media, that the Bill has been introduced in the Sri Lankan Parliament on 24.01.018 and its provisions were aimed at Indian Fishing Trawlers from Tamil Nadu, the Tamil Nadu fishermen, as well as their fishing gear, while they are peacefully fishing in their traditional fishing waters of Palk Bay. This new Bill has provisions to incarcerate our fishermen for longer periods of time and impose huge penalties, which run up to few crores of Indian rupees. The life and livelihood of our fishermen, who fish in the traditional waters of Palk Bay, will then be left at the mercy of the Sri Lankan Government. This move has created widespread resentment and panic amongst the fishermen of Tamil Nadu, especially amongst the fishermen fishing in the Palk Bay. It is an extremely unfortunate development, at the time when the Ministers of India and Sri Lanka met twice and the Joint Working Group on Fisheries met thrice, to work out a permanent solution to resolve this long pending sensitive livelihood issue. In addition, the Government of Tamil Nadu with the support of Government of India has initiated various proactive measures to decongest the Palk Bay and diversify the 2 trawling fishing effort form Palk Bay into deep sea fishing. This unilateral move by the Government of Sri Lanka has far reaching implications on the livelihood propositions of fishermen from Tamil Nadu and will definitely hamper proactive efforts taken by the State Government and the diplomatic efforts taken by the Government of India. 

Palk Bay is the historic and traditional fishing area of Indian fishermen from Tamil Nadu. Their historical rights were simply signed away, as part of the ill-advised Indo-Sri Lankan agreements of 1974 and 1976, which also unilaterally ceded Katchateevu to Sri Lanka, without having any foresight or concern for the plight of our innocent fishermen.

The stand of our revered Leader Puratchi Thalavi Amma and the Government of Tamil Nadu to abrogate the 1974 Indo Sri Lankan agreement that created an imaginary International Maritime Boundary Line and ceded the Katchatheevu islet along with the potential traditional fishing grounds of our fishermen to Sri Lanka, is sub-judice before the Supreme Court of India. Thus, it would be fitting for the Government of India to register its strong disapproval of such a move, affecting the livelihood of our fishermen in the Palk Bay, at the highest diplomatic level. 

I also wish to bring to the kind notice of the Government regarding the pathetic plight of fifteen fishermen from Kannyakumari, Tirunelveli and Thoothukudi Districts of Tamil Nadu, who were arrested and detained by the Iranian Coast Guard. These fishermen were engaged in fishing from the Emirate of Dubai fishing base. They ventured into sea for fishing on 22.10.2017 in two mechanized fishing boats and were apprehended by the Iranian Coast Guard on 24.10.2017, when they inadvertently strayed into Iranian waters. The apprehended fishermen are reportedly detained in their fishing boats in KISH Island, Iran for the past two months. It is ascertained that the Iranian Court imposed fine on these fishermen and the same has to be paid by the fishermen with the financial support their local sponsors from Dubai, UAE. It has been further reported that some of the fisherman needs medical intervention. The prolonged incarceration of these poor fishermen who went abroad for earning their humble livelihood, would severely affect their families and dependants in India. Hence, I urge upon the Union Government to intervene and instruct the Ambassadors of India in Tehran and United Arab Emirates to provide necessary medical attention and to take effective legal steps to secure the immediate release of these poor innocent fishermen from Tamil Nadu. I shall, therefore, urge upon the Union Government to take serious efforts to solve this vexed issue. 

As regards Swachchh Bharat Mission (SBM), despite wide awareness, the resistance to toilets in villages is considerable. Lack of adequate water/monitoring, unavailability of space, behavioural change are some of the reasons cited for creating hurdles in the success of the SBM. If these are issued, positive results will be looked up.

As regards Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY), the Government's target to provide road connectivity to every village by 2019 seems to be a distant dream. Lot of efforts are needed to expedite the process and to attain the desired objectives. Coming to the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY), as of January 2, 2018, only 9% of the sanctioned houses had been completed under PMAY-Urban and under PMAY-Gramin, only 22% of the target of 10 million houses has been completed. As the PMAY projects are progressing at a very slow pace, Government should focus to expedite the project in a speedy manner and by allocating adequate funds. 

As regards Chennai Metro Rail, Phase I of the CMRP covers a total length of 45 kms. Its extension from Washermenpet to Tiruvotriyur/Wimco Nagar covers further 9.51 kms. There is a need to substantially expand the CMRP like Delhi Metro. A detailed feasibility report for its expansion along three corridors has been approved by the State Government and included in the rolling plan of Japan International Cooperation Agency for funding. Our late leader, Puratchi Thalaivi Amma had requested the GOI to support the proposed Phase II of the CMRP so that the project is given early approval for commencement. I urge upon the Union Government to consider the State's request on top priority as the Chennai Metro is fast expanding and will ease the burden on road usage. 

*SHRI K. ASHOK KUMAR (KRISHNAGIRI): I would like to urge upon the Government to release of Rs 6,655 crores for the various centrally aided schemes due to Tamil Nadu. Tamil Nadu Education Department has not received Rs 4,474 crore from the Centre under various schemes in the last few years. Many education schemes, including post-metric scholarship for SC/ST students had suffered as the State was denied central funds on the ground of exhausting the budgetary allocations. A sum of Rs 1,547 crore has been pending towards the post-matric scholarship scheme for Scheduled Castes and Rs 27 crore for Scheduled Tribes for over a year. The Union Government has to pay arrears of Rs 1,312 crore for the Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA), the 'Education for All' scheme to Tamil Nadu. Under the Rashtriya Madhyamik Shiksha Abhiyan (RMSA), an amount of Rs 1,588-crore is due to be given to the State. I, therefore, urge upon the Union Government to expedite the release of all the funds due for Tamil Nadu without any delay.

In my Krishnagiri Constituency, Hosur SIPCOT is located. It is hardly 16 kilometres from Electronic City, Bengaluru. People from all walks of life, from IT professionals to workers of garment industry, more particularly women and contract workers, had to travel to and from daily through the 15 kilometres stretch between Mookandapalli (Hosur SIPCOT area) and Bommasandra Industrial area via Attepalli further to reach Electronics City. The road traffic is very badly affected by heavy vehicular congestion. It often takes an hour or more to pass this 15-20 kilometres stretch because of frequent traffic jams. If the Metro Rail is extended up to Mookandapalli, Hosur, it will be a boon for the people living in borders of both Tamil Nadu and Karnataka, as it will solve their daily traffic hurdles and facilitate them to reach their destinations easily. Commercially this will be very profitable too.

I urge the Government to extend the Metro rail services up to Mookandapalli, Hosur to facilitate thousands of people of all walks of life to have hassle free travel and to reach their working destinations quick and safe, cost effectively too.

In our country, 300 people are killed annually in human-elephant conflicts and hundreds are injured. The loss to elephants also is equally high and is on the rise. Hundreds of elephants get killed when they breach their territory. The invading elephants fall victim to humans and man-mad dangers like firing, attacking with spears and electrocution or killed in accidents by falling, speeding trains and trucks. Elephant-Human conflict occurs primarily due to encroachments of elephant passages and water bodies by human settlements. Elephants can cause heavy damages to standing crops amounting to a huge loss. This provokes a lethal retaliation against elephants. As a result, elephants are often killed.

In Krishnagiri District, Elephant-Human conflicts occur frequently. Elephants are naturally scared of honey bees. Elephants would quickly move away if they hear so much as the sound of a buzzing hive. Beehive fencing is a natural way to stop elephants invading the crops and habitation areas. It is easy to make and it cost very less compared to concrete barriers and electrified fences. People can benefit through the harvest and sale of honey. Bees can also increase biodiversity through pollination and even increase the yield of the crop that they protect. 

Therefore I urge the Government to promote and provide fund for beehive fences to keep elephants away from crops and human habitats and to save elephants from being victims in the Human-Elephant conflicts.

श्री आनंदराव अडसुल: माननीय उपाध्‍यक्ष जी, संविधान और परम्‍परा के अनुसार दोनों सदनों को महामहिम राष्‍ट्रपति जी संबोधित करते हैं। उस परम्‍परा को आगे बढ़ाते हुए, आज के महामहिम राष्‍ट्रपति जी ने दोनों सदनों को 29 जनवरी को साथ-साथ सम्‍बोधित किया। यह भी परम्‍परा रही है कि दोनों सदनों में उनके प्रति धन्‍यवाद प्रस्‍ताव पारित किया जाता है। मैं इस चर्चा में भाग लेते हुए अपनी तरफ से और हमारी पार्टी शिव सेना की तरफ से महामहिम राष्‍ट्रपति जी को धन्‍यवाद देना चाहता हूँ। साथ-साथ सम्‍मानीय प्रधान मंत्री जी का भी इसलिए अभिनंदन करना चाहता हूँ कि जो वित्‍त परिषद दावोस में हुई, 21 साल के बाद उनको वहां निमंत्रित किया गया। यहां तक कि उनके कर-कमलों से उसका उद्धाटन हुआ। एक बहुत बड़ा सम्‍मान हमें देश के प्रति महसूस हुआ। साथ-साथ 26 जनवरी को आसियान देशों के सभी प्रमुख उपस्‍थित थे। यह हमारे देश का गौरव है। देश की प्रतिष्‍ठा को दुनिया की चोटी पर ले जाने का काम माननीय प्रधानमंत्री जी ने जरूर किया है। इसलिए वह अभिनंदन के पात्र हैं। यहां राष्ट्रपति जी के अभिभाषण के कुछ बिन्‍दुओं पर जाने से पहले मैं एक और बिन्‍दु की तरफ जाना चाहता हूँ। जब पार्लियामेंट का 2014 का चुनाव प्रचार चालू था तो हमारे प्रधानमंत्री जी ने एक नारा दिया था- सबका साथ सबका विकास। तभी हम एन.डी.ए. के घटक दल साथ में थे। साथ में चुनाव लड़े और बहुत सालों के बाद एक परिवर्तन देश में आया। उस समय हम यह मानते थे कि एन.डी.ए. की सरकार प्रस्‍थापित हुई है। 

18 00 hrs

आगे-आगे चलते यह महसूस होने लगा कि नाम के लिए एनडीए सरकार है, लेकिन यह भाजपा रहित सरकार है, जिसका कारण यह है कि अगर हम ''सबका साथ सबका विकास'' का नारा देते हैं तो सभी को विश्‍वास में भी लेना जरूरी है। हमने यह अनुभव नहीं लिया। 23 जनवरी, 2018 को हमारे शिवसेना प्रमुख बाला साहेब का जन्‍म दिवस था। उस दिन हमारे पक्ष प्रमुख आदरणीय उद्धव जी ने एलान किया कि आगे आने वाले चुनाव हम अकेले लड़ेंगे।

HON.DEPUYY-SPEAKER: Now, the time is 6 o'clock.

THE MINISTER OF CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS AND MINISTER OF PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS (SHRI ANANTHKUMAR): Mr. Deputy Speaker, Sir, I request that the timing of the House be extended till the debate is over.

I want to inform, through you, that dinner has been arranged for all the hon. Members of Parliament in first floor Room no. 70, for media persons and officers at Room no. 73, and for staff at Room no. 74 from 8.30 onwards. Please continue the proceedings till the debate is over.

HON. DEPUTY-SPEAKER: The timing of the House has been extended. 

श्री आनंदराव अडसुल: हम यह देख रहे हैं कि जब से चर्चा शुरू हुई है तभी से ये वैल में खड़े हैं। इसका भी यह कारण है कि शायद उनको भी विश्‍वास में नहीं लिया है। मैं एक बात स्‍पष्‍ट रूप से सरकार के सामने रखना चाहता हूँ कि विश्‍वास एक ऐसी चीज है और दो वक्‍ताओं ने इसके पहले बताया कि पहले हमारा प्‍यार हमारी जनता की तरफ होना चाहिए और बाद में राजनीति आती है। दूसरी बात यह है कि जिसको साथ में लिया है, उसको विश्‍वास में भी लेनी चाहिए। हमारा कार्यकाल आगे जा रहा है, हमने गुजरात का चुनाव देखा है, हम उसके ज्‍यादा डिटेल में नहीं जाना चाहते हैं। हमने राजस्‍थान का उपचुनाव देखा है, यह सबक सिखाने वाली बातें हैं। हमारी लगन श्रद्धेय अटल, आडवाणी जी से लेकर भारतीय जनता पार्टी से एक प्रिंसिपल के ऊपर जरूर है और वह हिन्‍दुत्‍व है। हमारे शिवसेना प्रमुख मानते थे कि हिन्‍दुत्‍व राष्‍ट्रीयत्‍व है। दुर्भाग्‍य से कभी-कभी एक बात हमारे दिल में ठेस पहुंचाती है, पाकिस्‍तान जब भी हमारे देश का उल्‍लेख करता है तो 'हिन्‍दुस्‍तान' उल्‍लेख नहीं करते है, हम भारत इंडिया का उल्‍लेख करते हैं। यह भी एक दुर्भाग्‍य है। जो हिन्‍दुओं को स्‍थान है, उसको हिन्‍दुस्‍तान कहा जाताहै, अगर हम हिन्दू मेजॉरिटी में यहां रहते हैं, उसमें लाज और शर्म रखने की क्‍या जरूरत है। हम स्‍पष्‍ट रूप से सामने क्‍यों नहीं आते हैं? हम ने यह नारा सालों से दिया है कि ''राम मंदिर वहीं बनायोंगे लेकिन तारीख कभी नहीं बताएंगे'' आज आप में कमियां क्‍या हैं? पहले हमारे श्रद्धेय अटल जी की 25 पार्टी की सरकार थी तो मुश्‍किल थी। आज बहुत सालों के बाद हमारी सरकार आई है, आप खुद लोक सभा में मेजॉरिटी में हैं और साथ में हम भी हैं।

यदि कोई अच्‍छे इश्‍यूज हैं, तो हम आपके साथ हैं। आपने एक डेयरिंग ट्रिपल तलाक बिल लाकर की है। यह बिल लोक सभा में पास हो गया है और राज्‍य सभा में भी यह बिल जरूर पास हो जाएगा। खड़गे साहब ने बताया कि इसमें मदद करेंगे। राम जन्‍म भूमि की भी वही बात है।

आज हम महामहिम राष्‍ट्रपति महोदय के अभिभाषण पर लाए गए धन्‍यवाद प्रस्‍ताव पर चर्चा कर रहे हैं। यह भी परम्‍परा रही है कि उनका भाषण सरकार की तरफ से लिखा जाता है और सरकार के कार्य का यह आईना होता है। हमने देखा कि बहुत सी योजनाओं का प्रधान मंत्री जी द्वारा ऐलान किया गया जैसे स्‍टैंड-अप इंडिया, स्‍टार्ट-अप इंडिया, डिजिटल इंडिया, स्‍वच्‍छ भारत अभियान, जन-धन योजना, जन-औषधि योजना, प्रधान मंत्री फसल बीमा योजना, अटल बीमा योजना, बेटी पढ़ाओ बेटी बचाओ आदि अनेक योजनाएं हैं। हमारे साथी महताब जी ने आंकडों के साथ तथ्‍य प्रस्‍तुत किए हैं, लेकिन मैं बताना चाहता हूँ कि जब हम सभी अपने क्षेत्र में जाते हैं और किसी योजना को जमीनी स्‍तर पर देखते हैं, तो इन आंकड़ों का आपस में तालमेल दिखाई नहीं पड़ता है। उदाहरण के लिए मैं मुद्रा योजना की बात बताना चाहता हूँ। यह योजना बहुत अच्‍छी है कि बेरोजगार स्‍वयं अपना रोजगार करें। उसके लिए पचास हजार रुपये से लेकर दस लाख रुपये तक बिना कोलेट्रल सिक्‍योरिटी के लोन देने का प्रावधान है। इस योजना में दस लाख करोड़ रुपये का प्रावधान है लेकिन आज तक चार लाख करोड़ रुपये ही सैंक्‍शन हुए हैं। यह भी आशंका है कि सही मायने में चार लाख करोड़ रुपये भी वितरित हुए हैं या नहीं और उन बेरोजगारों ने रोजगार शुरू किया है या नहीं। मैं इसका इसलिए उल्‍लेख कर रहा हूँ क्‍योंकि जब हम अपने क्षेत्र में जाते हैं, तो ऐसे दो-चार उदाहरण हमें दिखाई देने चाहिए कि इन बेरोगार लोगों को लोन मिला है और इन्‍होंने यह रेाजगार किया है। ऐसे उदाहरण हमें अपने क्षेत्र में दिखाई नहीं देते हैं। ऐसी ही दूसरी भी योजनाएं हैं। हमारे राष्‍ट्रपति जी ने उल्‍लेख किया कि वर्ष 2016-17 में इकोनोमी स्‍लो डाउन हो गई। आंकड़ो के हिसाब से वर्ष 2015-16 में हमारी जीडीपी ग्रोथ रेट 8.2 परसेंट थी और वर्ष 2016-17 में हमारी जीडीपी ग्रोथ रेट 6.2 परसेंट पर आ गई।

इसके नीचे आने का क्‍या कारण है, इसमें कोई जाना नहीं चाहता है। डिमॉनिटाइजे़शन या नोट बंदी एलान की गयी, तो जहॉं तक मुझे जानकारी है, फरवरी, 2016 में रिज़र्व बैंक के गवर्नर से नोटबंदी के बारे में डिस्‍कस किया गया, इसका एलान करने के लिए कहा गया, लेकिन उन्‍होंने इसे नकार दिया। 8 नवम्‍बर, 2016 को अचानक रात को 8 बजे नोटबंदी का एलान किया गया। पाँच सौ और एक हजार रुपये के कितने नोट चलन से बाहर हुए? ये 86 पर्सेंट बाहर हुए। जब 86 पर्सेंट पाँच सौ और एक हजार के नोट चलन से बाहर होते हें, तो अचानक इतने पर्सेंट नोट तो वापस चलन में नहीं आ सकते हें और आये भी नहीं। इसका परिणाम यह हुआ कि चाहे छोटे व्‍यापारी हों, उद्योगपति हों, किसान हों, मजदूर हों, सभी के कारोबार पर उसका विपरीत परिणाम हुआ। यहाँ तक, आज की तिथि में 16 हजार करोड़ रुपये पाँच सौ और एक हजार रुपये के नोट अभी तक सरकार के पास या रिज़र्व बैंक के पास जमा नहीं हुए हैं। नये नोट छापने के लिए 30 हजार करोड़ रुपये सरकार का खर्च हुआ। इसलिए इकोनॉमी पर विपरीत असर होना बिल्‍कुल संभव है और वह हो गया है। यह भी हमें मानना पड़ेगा। इसलिए सही मायने में आप क्‍या करना चाहते हैं? अगर विश्‍वास में गवर्नर और कैबिनेट को लेते, तो शायद इसका यह परिणाम नहीं होता। आज भी क्या हो रहा है? जीएसटी भविष्य के लिए अच्छा है। इसे यूपीए सरकार भी लायी थी, लेकिन उस पर वे आगे नहीं बढ़ पाए। यह भविष्य के लिए अच्छा है, लेकिन शुरुआत में उसके क्या परिणाम हुए? हर महीने में, छोटे और बड़े व्यापारियों को रिटर्न फाइल करना पड़ता है। यदि एक घंटा भी रिटर्न फाइल करने में देरी हो गयी, तो भी फाइन लगाया गया। आर्थिक स्थिति में इसका बहुत ही विपरीत परिणाम हुआ। अचानक जब इस सरकार को महसूस हुआ, तो जो जीएसटी काउंसिल बनायी गयी है, उसने निर्णय दिया। अचानक निर्णय कैसे किया गया? जब गुजरात का चुनाव आया तो 214 कमोडिटीज के रेट नीचे किये गये। जो विभिन्न स्लैब्स बनाये गये थे, उनमें कमी की गयी, कई कमोडिटीज को पाँच पर्सेंट के स्लैब में रखा गया। यह खेल की बात नहीं है। यह बहुत ही सोच-समझकर करने की बात है। हम बड़े-बड़े एलान करते हैं, घोषणाऍं करते हैं, नारे देते हैं और योजनाएं लाते हैं। फिर घोटाले क्यों करते हैं? मैं यह इसलिए बताना चाहता हूँ क्योंकि हमने बहुत लोकप्रियता पायी है, हम आगे बढ़े हैं। दुनिया के स्तर बहुत ऊंचे जा चुके हैं। यदि हम अपने घर-परिवार में किसी को विश्वास में नहीं लेंगे, हकीकत में क्या होता है, माननीय उपाध्यक्ष जी, इस संबंध में मैं एक और बात बताना चाहता हूँ।

हमारे प्रधान मंत्री जी ने 'लेस गवर्नमेंट एंड मोर गवर्नेंस' का नारा दिया। योजनाएं कितनी भी अच्छी हों, उन पर अमल करना ब्यूरोक्रेसी के उपर निर्भर करता है। हम सबका यह अनुभव है, हमारे भाजपा के मेम्बर्स भी मानेंगे कि किसी भी अधिकारी के पास जाएंगे, तो सही समय पर सही काम नहीं होता है। यह मानना पड़ेगा।

उनको अधिकार ज्यादा देकर और खुद के अधिकार कम करके। इसलिए योजना कितनी भी अच्छी हो, उस पर अमल तभी होता है, जब सही मायने में ब्यूरोक्रेसी साथ देती है। लेकिन ऐसा नहीं होता है। सांसद आदर्श ग्राम योजना के तहत हम सभी को पहले साल में एक-एक गांव गोद लेने का कहा गया और हमने ले लिया। इससे हमें अनुभव क्या मिला? दो साल बीत चुके हैं और दूसरा गांव भी हमने गोद ले लिया है। इस साल तीसरा भी ले लिया है। हमें अनुभव हुआ है कि हर विभाग के अधिकारी क्या साथ देते है? यहां बैठे कितने लोग कहेंगे कि आदर्श ग्राम योजना का पूरा काम हो चुका है। कहीं 50, 60 और 70 प्रतिशत तक हुआ है। ऐसा हमारा अनुभव है। लेकिन ऐसा क्यों है? हम भी इस बात का जानते हैं कि यह योजना अच्छी है। हमें गांवों का आदर्श बनाना है। लेकिन ब्यूरोक्रेसी साथ नहीं देती है। क्या कभी सरकार ने वहां जाकर देखा है कि जो हमने ऐलान किया था, उस हिसाब से काम हो रहा है या नहीं? 

स्किल डेवलपमेंट का नारा दिया गया और इसके लिए एक मंत्रालय भी अलग से बनाया गया। हमारे रुडी जी को मंत्री बनाया गया था। बह बहुत काबिल थे, हम उनकी सराहना भी करते थे। मुझे अन्य बातों में नहीं जाना है। लेकिन हमारे सामने एक बात सामने आयी। डीपीडीसी की मीटिंग होती है जो जिला स्तर पर होती है। उस मीटिंग में सांसद भी बैठते हैं। हमने पूछा कि स्किल डेवलपमेंट के कितने सेंटर्स हमारे जिले में हैं। उन्होंने कहा कि 150 है। हमने कहा कि कहां-कहां है? उन्होंने कुछ के नाम बताए। हमने कहा कि हम वहां जाकर देखना चाहते है। उन्होंने कहा कि वहां अभी कोई नहीं होगा। बाद में पता चला कि स्किल डेवलपमेंट का काम एनजीओज़ को दिया गया था। ये एनजीओज़ एक रजिस्टर बनाते हैं, एक बेरोजगार को पकड़ते हैं, उससे सिग्नेचर लेते हैं, महीने में डेढ़ हजार मिलते हैं, उसको पांच सौ रुपये देते हैं और एक हजार रुपये अपने जेब में डालते हैं। इस तरह से वे उससे तीसे दिन का सिग्नेचर लेते हैं। मैं आप लोगों का यह हकीकत बता रहा हूँ। मैं किसी के ऊपर आरोप नहीं लगा रहा हूँ। सरकार को यह बताना जरुरी है कि हमारी योजना का क्या हो रहा है? हमने कितने लोगों को प्लेसमेंट दिया है? कितने लोग ट्रैन्ड हुए है? मेरे इलाके में कए ट्राइबल एरिया है। मैं वहां एक क्लस्टर लाना चाहता था, जहां हनी और मावा बने। क्योंकि ट्राइबल एरिया में उनको उसका सही भाव नहीं मिलता है। अगर सही तरीके से उसका पैकेज करके उसको बेचा जाए तो उसकी जापान में बहुत डिमांड है। इसलिए हमने मंत्री जी को वहां योजना शुरु करने के लिए प्रपोज़ल उनके सामने रखा, जिस पर उन्होंने हां कहा था। हम तरह से एक प्रोजेक्ट लेकर आए। हमने ट्राइबल एरिया के बेरोजगार सौ-डेढ़ सौ लोगों से कॉन्टैक्ट किया। उनको हमने बताया कि हम आपको हनी उत्पादन के लिए ट्रेनिंग देना चाहते हैं, उसके लिए ड्रैस देना चाहते हैं और हमेशा के लिए रोजगार देना चाहते हैं। उन्होंने कहा कि हमें पहले भी पांच सौ रुपये मिलते थे, आप भी हमें पांच सौ रुपये दीजिए तब हम सोचेंगे कि आपके प्रोग्राम में हमे आना है या नहीं? यह आदत क्यों पड़ी? उन्होंने हमारे साथ ऐसा बर्ताव क्यों किया? उनका अनुभव ऐसा था कि रजिस्टर पर सिग्नेचर करने से पांच सौ रुपये मिलते हैं और तीस दिन तक सिग्नेचर करना है। यह एक गलत आदत उनको पड़ी हम कुछ अच्छा करना चाहते है, कुछ अलग करना चाहते हैं, जिसके बारे में किसी के दिमाग में नहीं आया था। योजना का नाम बहुत आकर्षक होता है। योजना के पर्टिकुलर्स भी बहुत अच्छे होते हैं, लेकिन योजना पर अमल होता है या नहीं, इस पर हमारी कोई निगरानी नहीं होती है। यह हमारा दुर्भाग्य है। इसलिए शायद हमारे साथी लोगों को लगता होगा कि हमेशा सरकार का जमकर साथ देने वाले, विरोधियों का विरोध करने वाले आज ऐसी बात क्यों बोल रहे हैं?

मैं निष्पक्ष बात कर रहा हूँ। मैं दोनों तरफ से बात कर रहा हूँ। जो गलत है, वह गलत है और जो सही है, वह सही है, यह हमारे शिव सेना प्रमुख बाला साहब ने बताया।

महोदय, हमारा इतना कम समय है। यह क्या बात है, यहाँ लोगों ने एक-एक घंटे बात की है। मुझे भी जानकारी है, कभी-कभी सौभाग्य से मैं आपके यहाँ बैठता हूँ।

जो अच्छी बातें होती हैं, उनकी हम जरुर सराहना करते हैं। जो आधार कार्ड के माध्यम से चार सौ योजनाओं के पैसे सही लोगों के पास पहुंचे हैं और 54 हजार करोड़ रुपये की बचत हुई है, ऐसी चीजों की सराहना करनी चाहिए और हम इसकी जमकर सराहना करते हैं। जो अच्छी बात है, उसकी सराहना करनी चाहिए। प्रधान मंत्री सुरक्षा बीमा योजना के माध्यम से एक रुपये प्रतिमाह में दो लाख रुपये का बीमा मिलता है। किसी परिवार का कोई व्यक्ति गुजर जाता है तो उससे इस परिवार को दो लाख रुपये मिलते हैं। इसका प्रीमियम एक रुपया प्रतिमाह है। आज 31 करोड़ परिवारों ने अपना खाता बैंक में खोला है। उन्होंने केवल यह लिखकर दिया है कि मेरे 12 रुपये एक रुपये एक साल के लिए काट लीजिए तो वह बीमा उन पर लागू होता है। अटल बीमा योजना है, जो हमारे बुजुर्ग हैं, यह उनके लिए है। यह अच्छी योजना है। मैं अंत में यही बताना चाहता हूँ, आपने घंटी बजा दी है, मैं दूसरी घंटी नहीं सुनना चाहता हूँ योजनाएं अच्छी होने से कुछ नहीं होता है, अगर उन योजनाओं का अमल अच्छा होता है तो सरकार के प्रति जनता का विश्वास बढ़ता है। ये योजनाएं अगर जनता के भले के लिए बनाई जाती हैं, प्यार से इन्हें लागू करते हैं तो जनता उनके साथ हमेशा के लिए रहती है। सबका साथ तभी मिलेगा, जब विकास सबका होगा। इसे उल्टा करना पड़ेगा कि सबका विकास, इसलिए सबका साथ, यही बोलकर मैं अपनी वाणी को विराम देता हूँ।

*डाँ करण सिंह यादव (अलवर): महोदया, इस महान सदन में एक बार फिर उपचुनाव में जीत कर आने से मैं अपने आपको भाग्‍यशाली एवं गर्वित महसूस करता हूं। 

मुझे खेद व्‍यक्‍त करना पड़ता है कि माननीय राष्‍ट्रपति जी से सरकार ने पुन: जुमलों व कभी नहीं पूर्ण होने वाली घोषणायें करवाने का प्रयास किया है। 

आज देश कर हर तबका हताश व परेशान है। गरीब और गरीब होता जा रहा है तथा देश के चंद लोग जिनकी गिनती सैकड़ों में ही आती है, वे दिनों-दिन और समृद्ध एवं मालामाल हुए जा रहे हैं। हर वर्ग चाहे व्‍यापारी हो, किसान हो, मजदूर हो, युवा हो, अल्‍पसंख्‍यक हो अथवा दलित हो, अपने आपको ठगा हुआ महसूस करते हैं। भाजपा नेतृत्‍व की इस सरकार में देश भर में किसान आत्‍महत्‍या कर रहे हैं। अभिभाषण में जहां किसान की आमदनी डेढ़ गुनी अथवा दोगुनी करने की बात की जा रही है, लेकिन हकीकत यह है कि किसान कंगाली की ओर अग्रसर है। किसान को अपनी फसल के समुचित मूल्‍य नहीं मिल पा रहे हैं। सरकार समर्थन मूल्‍य की घोषणा तो करती है मगर कहीं भी सरकारी खरीद अथवा क्रय केन्‍द्र नहीं खोले जा रहे हैं। सरसों का समर्थन मूल्‍य तो 3700 रूपये प्रति क्‍विंटल घोषित किया गया है, मगर सरकारी एजेंसियों द्वारा खरीद नहीं किये जाने से मंडियां में किसान को औने-पौने दामों पर अपनी फसल बेचनी पड़ती है। 3700 रूपये समर्थन मूल्‍य की सरसों 3300-3400 रूपये प्रति क्‍विंटल पर बिकती है। 1400 रूपये समर्थन मूल्‍य का बाजरा राजस्‍थान में किसान को 1000-1100 रूपये प्रति क्‍विंटल पर बेचना पड़ता है।

हर साल बिजली की दरें बढ़ती हैं। डीजल की कीमत लगातार बढ़ रही है। खाद-बीज के भाव महंगे हो गए हैं। नतीजा यह होता है कि किसान कर्जदार बना रहता है। राजस्‍थान के कोटा सम्‍भाग में इस बार लहुसन की अच्‍छी फसल हुई, मगर सरकार की अनदेखी के कारण बहुत कम भाव पर फसल बेचने के बाद किसान आत्‍महत्‍या करने को मजबूर हैं।

युवा व शिक्षित बेरोजगारों की संख्‍या दिनों-दिन बढ़ती जा रही है। सरकार के 1-2 करोड़ रोजगार के वादे झूठे साबित हुए हैं। नोटबंदी में जीएसटी की मार से औद्योगिक इकाइयां बंद होने लग गई हैं। जो फैक्‍ट्रियां तीन शिफ्ट में चलती थीं, वे दो शिफ्ट में आ गईं और जो दो शिफ्ट में चलती थीं, वे एक शिफ्ट में आ गई हैं। बेरोजगार युवा आपराधिक गतिविधियों की ओ जा रहा है।

देश में चिकित्‍सा व्‍यवस्‍था चरमरा गई है। सरकारी अस्‍पतालों की दुर्दशा है। कुछ सरकारें जैसे राजस्‍थान सरकार, सरकारी डिस्‍पेंसरियों एवं प्राथमिक स्‍वास्‍थ्‍य केंद्रों को निजी व्‍यवसाइयों को सौंप रही है। 

सरकारी उदासीनता का जीता-जागता उदाहरण अलवर में 800 करोड़ से निर्मित ईएसआईसी अस्‍पताल गत चार वर्षों से खाली पड़ा है। यूपीए-वन एवं यूपीए-टू में ईएसआईसी के इस बड़े अस्‍पताल में मेडिकल कॉलेज चलना था। भाजपा सरकार ने आते ही इस अस्‍पताल व मेडिकल से नाता तोड़ दिया। गत चार वर्षों से 800 करोड़ रूपये के 500 बिस्‍तर के अस्‍पताल में ताले लगे हैं। आठ-दस चौकीदार देखभाल करते हैं, अस्‍पताल की बिल्‍डिंग में चमगादड़ निवास करते हैं। यह है सरकार की चिकित्‍सा के प्रति जवाबदेही ।

देश व विशेष तौर पर राजस्‍थान पीने व सिंचाई के पानी से त्रस्‍त है। केन्‍द्र सरकार व राज्‍य सरकार ने अलवर में चंबल से पीने के पानी की पूर्ववर्ती सरकार की योजना को ठंडे बस्‍ते में डाल दिया है। 

स्‍पष्‍ट है कि 2019 में जनता सबक सिखाएगी। हर बात में 2022 तक का वादा करना जनता की भावनाओं के साथ खिलवाड़ है । 

*डाँ रघु शर्मा (अजमेर): संसद के समक्ष भारत के महामहिम राष्‍ट्रपति महोदय द्वारा दिये गये भाषण में भाजपा सरकार की जो तथाकथित उपलब्धियां गिनाई गई हैं, वह इस देश के करोड़ों लोगों को सिर्फ सब्‍जबाग दिखाने के अलावा कुछ भी नहीं है। यह सरकार जुमलों से बनी तथा जुमलों से ही चल रही है। देश का आम आदमी इनकी वायदा खिलाफी से ठगा सा महसूस कर रहा है। बेरोजगारों को प्रतिवर्ष दो करोड़ रोजगार देने का वायदा करके सत्‍ता में आई भाजपा सरकार ने इस देश के कोटि-कोटि बेरोजगार नौजवानों को निराश किया है। सरकार रोजगार देने के मामले में फिसड्डी साबित हुई है। महंगाई कम करने का वायदा करके सत्‍ता में आई भाजपा सरकार ने देश की जनता को निराश किया है। जब से इस देश में भाजपा सरकार बनी है तब से महंगाई तीन-चार गुना बढ़ गई है। गरीब आदमी का जीना मुश्‍किल हो गया है। गरीबों के लिए यूपीए सरकार द्वारा चलाई गई मनरेगा सहित अन्‍य कई कल्‍याणकारी योजनाओं को भाजपा सरकार ने अघोषित रूप से बंद सा करके गरीबों के मुंह से निवाला छीना है। देश में किसान निरंतर आत्‍महत्‍या कर रहे हैं तथा भाजपा की असंवेदनशील सरकार इस देश के किसानों को बचाने के लिए भी कुछ नहीं कर रही है। भाजपा सरकार नौजवान विरोधी, आम आदमी विरोधी, गरीब विरोधी एवं किसान विरोधी साबित हुई है। इस सरकार ने देश के हर वर्ग को निराशा के अलावा कुछ नहीं दिया है। मेरे निर्वाचन क्षेत्र अजमेर में यूपीए सरकार के द्वारा किशनगढ़ एयरपोर्ट की जो सौगात दी गई थी, आज भी वहां की जनता को उक्‍त सेवाओं का लाभ नहीं मिल पा रहा है। 161 करोड़ रूपये भारत सरकार के खर्च हो जाने के बावजूद जनता को उसका लाभ नहीं मिला। यह भाजपा सरकार की अकर्मण्‍यता है। इसी प्रकार अजमेर से कोटा तथा अजमेरे से सवाई माधोपुर तक के लिए रेलवे सेवा से जोड़ने हेतु जो कदम यूपीए सरकार ने उठाये थे, वह काम वहीं का वहीं रूका हुआ है। यह मेरे क्षेत्र की जनता के साथ भाजपा सरकार द्वारा किया गया अन्‍याय है। मैं सरकार से आग्रह करूँगा कि वह जुमलेबाजी से ऊपर उठकर धरातल पर भी कुछ काम करके दिखाये,जिससे इस क्षेत्र के लोगों में भाजपा सरकार के खिलाफ जो निराशा व्‍याप्‍त है, वह कुछ हद तक दूर हो सके। 

भाजपा सरकार हर मोर्चे पर विफल सरकार साबित हुई है। यह आकंठ घमंड में डूबी हुई सरकार है, जिसका जनहित से अब तक कोई सरोकार नहीं रहा है। 

मैं सरकार से कहना चाहूंगा कि वह इस देश की जनता को सब्‍जबाग दिखाने से बाज आये एवं हकीकत के धरातल पर भी कुछ काम करके दिखाये, वरना इस देश की जनता भाजपा को 2019 में करारा जवाब देगी। हर बात एवं हर मुद्दे पर यह सरकार 2022 एवं 2024 का हवाला देकर फिर से देश को गुमराह कर रही है। धन्‍यवाद। 

*SHRIMATI KOTHAPALLI GEETHA (ARAKU): I wholeheartedly congratulate His Excellency, President of India, Dr. Ramanath Kovind on his first Address to the Joint session of the Parliament. I thank the Hon'ble President for starting his speech with an emphasis on inclusiveness, 'Vasudhaiva Kutumbham' and the vision of New India and remembering the words of our Dr. Baba Saheb Ambedkar, "Political democracy cannot survive without social and economic democracy".

The Hon'ble President has mentioned in detail different issues pertaining to the policies and priorities of the Union Government like economy and finance, defence and security, governance and legal reforms, education, health, social justice and empowerment, women and child development, labour, industry and manufacturing, transport and connectivity, energy, urban and rural development, agriculture and water resources, science and technology and development of the north east areas.

Agriculture is the backbone of Indian economy and the farmers of the country are subject to hardships and are ending their lives as they are unable to bear the losses. It is the responsibility of the Government to immediately frame an action plan to rescue the farmers from hardships. The Government has provided them with various schemes to double the income as the Government has decided to achieve this ambitious target by 2022.

Unemployment is a major aspect which is a biggest challenge before the Government. Unemployment is the greatest economic challenge facing India. Virtually, all major economic policy issues derive this central challenge. The population of our country is ever-rising. The abnormal rise in population has intensified the problem of unemployment in India. That is why the problem of employment has been getting more and more acute every year. 

United Nations’ International Labour Organisation (ILO) released its 2017 World Employment and Social Outlook report, which says "Unemployment in India is projected to increase from 17.7 million last year to 17.8 million in 2017 and 18 million next year. In percentage terms, unemployment rate will remain at 3.4 percent in the year 2017-18" which is very alarming and needs immediate attention of the Government to evolve a platform to resolve this situation.

Working for the upliftment and dignity of all weaker sections is a very important task of the Government. I appreciate the Government's initiative in forming a National Commission for the Backward Classes. The initiatives taken to support the tribal communities are also commendable. Providing of Minimum Support Price to the several forest produce will also empower the tribal population who are dependent for their living on the forest produce. 

Though the Government has been implementing the schemes for strengthening the economic democracy, the schemes are actually suffering and lag in the implementation stages. The MUDRA scheme, Prime Ministers flagship program, which is aimed to support poor and middle class to establish small business and create self employment opportunities and to create self sustainability is also not reachable to the vulnerable classes.

I sincerely appreciate the Government in the stand taken in providing security and dignity to the Muslim women by tabling the Triple Talaq Bill. I request the Union Government to move a step forward in extending this attitude to promote women literacy and extend the program of 'Beti Bachao, Beto Padhao' extensively across the country.

In the said spirit, I also request the Union Government to introduce the Women reservation Bill in the Parliament which has been long pending to encourage the women into the legislative bodies and provide equal opportunity.

I sincerely appreciate the efforts of the Government in creating economic security to the poor and senior citizens. It is also the responsibility of the Union Governments to ensure to end pint delivery mechanism. Due to the federal structure of the country, implementation of the policies depends on the commitment both from the State and the Central Government. The Union Government has to ensure that all the schemes and policies announced are being carried out in true spirit.

The effort of the Government in making India ‘Swatch Bharat’ is highly commendable and has also created a sensitisation across the masses in the country. Providing electricity under the 'Saubhagya Scheme' will light many lives. Regarding road connectivity, I thank the Union Government for their emphasis on providing connectivity to every village and this step will have far-reaching consequences in the implementation of the welfare programs as well as in the areas of education and health. Particularly in tribal areas like my constituency Araku, wherein people have been suffering from decades due to connectivity issues, this initiative is a boon. But the implementation is very slow and the State Governments are not as keen as the Central Government and there is a huge delay due to the lethargic attitude of the officers.

To simplify the procedures, we appreciate the Government’s initiative in repealing the obsolete laws. I feel that the Government should also come up and amend the reservations and make the reservations available only to the vulnerable removing the advantage to the creamy layer, who are only enjoying the benefit of reservations. 

I firmly feel that the Government should frame stringent laws against the corrupt practices and raise the whip on the corrupt officials. Though many cases have been filed by the ACB of the States, the punishment given is not even for one percent and the rest are escaping the legal process and are getting reinstated without any punishment. Such tendency of the Government will create unrest among the people of the nation and also make them lose faith in the Government.

At this juncture, I would also like to quote the situation of my State of Andhra Pradesh, wherein the people are subjected to so much of hardships due to the reorganization of the State which happened arbitrarily. The demand for the railway zone is pending since the past 3 years and the industrial corridor that has been announced from Visakhapatnam to Chennai is yet to start off. The issue of Tribal University has also been long pending and I request that steps to be taken to complete this at the earliest.

Finally, I would like to close by quoting our Hon'ble Prime Minister Narendra Modiji's words "Good Governance is treating development as a mass movement in order to see the fruits of development reach the poor and the downtrodden". With these words I would like convey my thanks to His Excellency, the President of India for his kind address to the joint houses of Parliament.

*श्री बीरेद्र कुमार चौधरी (झंझारपुर) :  मैं महामहिम राष्‍ट्रपति  महोदय जी के माननीय प्रधानमंत्री श्री नरेंद्र मोदी जी के द्वारा देश के सर्वांगीण विकास के लिए किए गए कार्यों का वर्णन किए इसके लिए महामहिम राष्‍ट्रपति  जी को धन्यवाद देता हूं। 

गरीबों, किसानों और वरिष्‍ठ  अधिकारियों के जीवन में आर्थिक सुधार की भावना को दूर करने के लिए मेरी सरकार संवेदनशील एवं सक्रिय है। 

समाज के प्रत्येक कमजोर एवं वंचित वर्ग का उत्थान एवं सम्मान मेरी सरकार की प्राथमिकता है, सरकार ने पिछड़े वर्ग में भी अति पिछड़े वर्ग को उच्च शिक्षा और नियुक्तियों में लाभ सुलभ कराने के लिए पिछड़े वर्ग के उप श्रेणी के कारण के माध्यम हेतु आयोग का गठन किया गया है। जिसके लिए मैं सरकार को कोटि-कोटि धन्यावाद देता हूं। 

मेरी सरकार, समाज के हर तबके तक विकास पहुंचाने की इसी सोच के साथ ""प्रधानमंत्री ग्रामीण सड़क योजना"" का कार्य और तेजी से आगे बढ़ा रही है। 2014 में केवल 56 प्रतिशत गांव ही सड़क संपर्क से जुड़े थे। 

अब 82 प्रतिशत से ज्यादा गांव सड़कों से जुड़ चुके हैं जिनमें से अधिकांश दूर-दराज और दुर्गम इलाकों में हैं। हमारा लक्ष्य देश के प्रत्येक गांव को सड़क संपर्क से जोड़ देने का है। 

मेरी सरकार ने "सीखों और कमाओं" उस्ताद "गरीब नवाज कौशल विकास योजना" "नई रोशनी" आदि कार्यक्रमों के जरिए मुस्लिम, इसाई, सिख, बौध, पारसी एवं जैन समाज के युवाओं को रोजगार के अवसर दिए गए हैं। 

माननीय प्रधानमंत्री जी ने सभी के सर पर छत हो, ओर उसे पानी-बिजली-शौचालय की सुविधा मिले, इस संवेदनशील सोच के साथ मेरी सरकार देश के हर आवासहीन गरीब परिवार को वर्ष  2022 तक घर उपलब्ध कराने के लक्ष्य पर काम कर रही है। 

हमारे देश की सांस्कृतक परम्पराएं, हमारी पहचान है और "एक भारत-श्रेष्‍ठ  भारत" की भावना को आधार देती है। 

देश में पहली बार ऐसा अवसर आया है जब देश में बिजली क्षमता के विस्तार में लक्ष्य से अधिक बढ़ोतरी हुई है। अब भारत बिजली का नेट एक्सपोर्टर बन गया है। 

धन्यवाद। 

*SHRI S.P. MUDDAHANUME GOWDA (TUMKUR): The President's Speech is normally treated as the agenda of the Union Government for the year for which the Hon. President makes his speech. The Union Government sets the nation on its path for the current year. At least in the President's Address, the programmes of the Union Government are made known. A plain reading of the Speech should create confidence among the people of this country. But, unfortunately, we could not see the probable action plan of the Union Government that would create a right path for the welfare of the people of this country.

In the President's Address, we can see only theoretical mentioning of some of the programmes of the Union Government. We are not able to find the way that the Government can take for implementation of the programmes. 

Farmers are in distress in the country. What is required is the way by which the farmers can be saved from the present crisis. The present programmes available in the Union Government are insufficient to save the farmers from the present situation. Consistent suicides being committed by the farmers in the whole country is an insulting factor be it for the Union Government or the respective States. 

The Union Government talks about the welfare of farmers. They should first try to understand the reasons for the suicides of the farmers. The major reasons that could be seen all over the country are (i) failure of the crops frequently, (ii) insufficient price they get on the agricultural products they grow, (iii) insufficient minimum support price during the period of crises, (iv) failure to provide good marketing facilities, and (v) bank loans which cannot be repaid due to the above reasons resulting in accumulation of debt.

Farmers in the State of Karnataka were also facing the above said problems. They were not in a position to repay the loans they raised through the co-operative institutions. Hence the State Government waived the farmers' loan taken from the co-operative institutions. But, they are not a in a position to get the farmers' loan waived which were taken from Commercial Banks. Once, the Union Government in UPA-II took the decision to waive the farmers’ loan taken from the commercial banks to the tune of Rs. 72,000 crores. 

People of the country, particularly the farmers, were anticipating that the Union Government will show some path, that too a welfare path, for the farmers to come out of the prevailing situation and stop the farmers' suicides. That is to say, the President should have mentioned about the present crises in the farming sector and the remedial measures being taken for the welfare of the farmers.

Hon'ble President has mentioned about holding simultaneous elections for both Parliament and State Assemblies. Some concrete decision is to be taken in this regard by taking not only the political parties but also the States into confidence. 

Since the intention of the Union Government with regard to holding simultaneous elections is clear, now they have to come out and make the country know about the status of those States where elections to assemblies were held very recently. Because of this, people are under utter confusion. Hence the Union Government should come out with the actual action plan in this regard. 

Viewing from any angle, the vision of the Union Government is not clear about the action plan for the current year, which could have been seen in the President's Address.

The President in his Address has raised many issues with regard to the programmes initiated by this Government.
